title: Independent work: GCD and LCM
summary: No scaffolding. Implement greatest common divisor against provided tests, then least common multiple with tests you write yourself — checked by hidden acceptance tests.

steps.title: Greatest common divisor

checks.label: gcd_test.cpp is part of the calc_tests target

hints: Declare `long long gcd(long long a, long long b);` in calc.h and define it in calc.cpp. Add tests/gcd_test.cpp to calc_tests in CMakeLists.txt.
Euclid noticed that any number dividing both `a` and `b` also divides `a % b` (the remainder). So gcd(a, b) == gcd(b, a % b). What is gcd(a, 0)?
Negative inputs: the GCD is defined as non-negative. Make both inputs non-negative first.

steps.title: Least common multiple — your tests, hidden tests

checks.label: Hidden acceptance tests pass
checks.failMessage: Your tests pass, but the hidden acceptance tests found a case your lcm gets wrong. Which edge cases haven't you tested yet?

hints: Think about zero, negative numbers, and what happens to `a * b` when both are close to the largest `long long`.
`a / gcd(a, b) * b` computes the same value without the oversized intermediate product.
